Cadence plays Pong

One belief patch that learned the game from pixels and actions. Every plan is imagined from the live belief; nothing recorded is fed to the rollouts.

Model card

What you see

Left: the frame each decision was made from, under it the retina the brain read, and beside that the retina it expected to see 1, 4 and 8 decisions ahead along the plan it chose. Right: the belief the plans were imagined from, one dot per channel, and every candidate plan with its reads.

At each decision the belief patch imagines every plan, one action held for decisions, from its live belief with no future input. It reads the reward and the danger along each plan, ranks the plans by reward minus times danger, executes the first action of the best plan, then assimilates what the game shows. A decision holds for four emulated frames.

The model

The brain is one Cadence belief patch; the retina is the 84 by 84 grey preprocessing every pixel learner on the Atari bench shares.
